'''Brandon Clarke''' (September 19, 1996 – May 11, 2026) was a Canadian–American professional basketball player who served as a [[power forward]] for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State Spartans]] and the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. Clarke was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the 21st overall pick and then immediately traded to the Grizzlies. He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] in 2020. In June 2026, ''[[Complex Networks|Complex]] Canada'' placed Clarke 20th in their ranking of ''The 20 Best Canadian Basketball Players of All Time''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wavvy |first=Mr. |date=2026-06-04 |title=The 20 Best Canadian Basketball Players of All Time, Ranked |url=https://www.complex.com/sports/a/mr-wavvy/best-canadian-basketball-players-all-time-ranked |access-date=2026-08-14| website=Complex |language=en}}</ref> 

==Early life==
Brandon Clarke was born on September 19, 1996, in [[Vancouver]], British Columbia, to a Canadian mother, Whitney Triplett, and a Jamaican father, Steve Clarke.<ref>[https://andscape.com/features/grizzlies-brandon-clarke-bonds-with-dad-during-trip-to-civil-rights-museum/ Grizzlies’ Brandon Clarke bonds with dad during trip to civil rights museum]</ref> At age three, Clarke moved with his family to the U.S. city of [[Phoenix, Arizona]]. He eventually became a [[dual citizen]] of Canada and the U.S.<ref>{{cite web|last=Crumpacker|first=John |title=Brandon Clarke Bolstering Bulldogs |url=https://wccsports.com/news/2018/12/14/mens-basketball-crumpacker-brandon-clarke-bolstering-bulldogs.aspx.aspx|date=December 14, 2018 |publisher=West Coast Conference|access-date=April 9, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Carlan|last=Gay|title=NBA Draft 2019: The world may not have known it, but Brandon Clarke has always been a proud Canadian|date=July 16, 2019|website=NBA.com|url=https://ca.nba.com/news/nba-draft-2019-the-world-may-not-have-known-it-but-brandon-clarke-has-always-been-a-proud-canadian/1rm467x7rlntz1bk3f031ixonk|access-date=December 28, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107230932/https://ca.nba.com/news/nba-draft-2019-the-world-may-not-have-known-it-but-brandon-clarke-has-always-been-a-proud-canadian/1rm467x7rlntz1bk3f031ixonk|archive-date=November 7, 2020}}</ref>

Clarke attended [[Desert Vista High School]] in Phoenix.<ref>{{cite news |last=Prehm |first=Matt |title=Oregon makes final three for big-time basketball transfer |url=https://247sports.com/college/oregon/article/oregon-makes-final-three-for-big-time-basketball-transfer-106469710/ |access-date=September 27, 2018 |work=247Sports |date=August 24, 2017 }}</ref> He was named an All-Arizona Division 1 honoree by the ''[[Arizona Republic]]'' after leading Desert Vista to the championship game in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=SJSUSpartans.com - Brandon Clarke Bio - San Jose State University Official Athletic Site Men's Basketball |url=http://www.sjsuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/brandon_clarke_972548.html |website=SJSUSpartans.com |access-date=September 27, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928044242/http://www.sjsuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/brandon_clarke_972548.html |archive-date=September 28, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Clarke attended [[San Jose State University]] and played two seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|Spartans]]. As a [[freshman]], he was named [[Mountain West Conference]] Sixth Man of the Year after averaging 10.1 points and 7.3 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] in conference play.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kktv.com/content/news/MOUNTAIN-WEST-ANNOUNCES-2015-16-MENS-BASKETBALL-ALL-CONFERENCE-TEAM-371490681.html|title=MOUNTAIN WEST ANNOUNCES 2015-16 MEN’S BASKETBALL ALL-CONFERENCE TEAM|work=KKTV|date=March 8, 2016 |access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref> As a [[sophomore]], he averaged 17.3 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.6 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] and 2.3 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] on route to being named an All-Mountain West First Team and an Mountain West All-Defensive Team honoree.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://themw.com/news/2017/03/07/58bef2c9e4b0a831fd2875ff-131372573347289037-2/|title=Mountain West Announces 2016-17 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team|work=Mountain West Conference|date=March 7, 2017|access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref>

After the season, he transferred to [[Gonzaga University]] to play for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Bulldogs]]. He [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brandon Clarke -2017-18 Men's Basketball Roster - Gonzaga University |url=https://gozags.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=326 |website=GoZags |access-date=September 27, 2018}}</ref> In his [[junior (education year)|junior]] season, Clarke continued onward with his improvements and was named the [[West Coast Conference]]'s (WCC) Newcomer of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and was named a member of the All-WCC First Team. Clarke was the first player in WCC history to win both their Newcomer of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year honors in the same season.<ref>{{cite press release|title=WCC Announces 2018-19 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2019/3/5/wcc-announces-2018-19-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx|access-date=March 5, 2019|publisher=West Coast Conference |date=March 5, 2019}}</ref> He was also named a third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by ''[[The Sporting News]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/sporting-news-2018-19-college-basketball-all-americans/iiljzskqnbtt1g4c298897sra|title=Sporting News' 2018-19 college basketball All-Americans|work=The Sporting News|date=March 13, 2019|first=Mike|last=DeCourcy|access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref> On March 23, 2019, Clarke recorded a career-high 36 points alongside eight rebounds, five blocks and three assists in an 83–71 win over No. 9 seeded [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]]. He became the third player in [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] history to record a game with at least 35 points and five blocks, joining [[Shaquille O'Neal]] and [[David Robinson]]. Clarke also broke a team record in points scored in an NCAA tournament game, breaking a record previously set by [[Adam Morrison]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/apr/17/gonzagas-brandon-clarke-declares-for-nba-draft/|title=Gonzaga’s Brandon Clarke declares for NBA draft|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=April 17, 2019|first=Jim|last=Meehan|access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |last=Faraudo |first=Jeff |user=JeffFaraudo |number=1109628490096078849 |date=March 23, 2019 |title=Nice company: Brandon Clarke 1 of 3 players with 35 points and 5 blocked shots in an NCAA tournament game. The others: Shaquille O'Neal and David Robinson. |language=en |access-date=June 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190408061406/https://twitter.com/jefffaraudo/status/1109628490096078849 |archive-date=April 8, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Memphis Grizzlies (2019–2026)===
Clarke was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the 21st overall pick. On July 7, 2019, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] announced that they had officially acquired the rights to Clarke from the Thunder for the draft rights to [[Darius Bazley]] and a future second-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies acquire draft rights to Brandon Clarke from Thunder Memphis trades draft rights to Darius Bazley and future second round draft pick to Oklahoma City; Grizzlies sign Clarke to multi-year contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-draft-rights-to-brandon-clarke-from-thunder-190707|date=July 7, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> With four [[double-double]]s, he was named the [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of the [[2019 NBA Summer League]], becoming the second non-American to win the award. He had 15 points, 16 rebounds, 4 assists and 3 blocks in the championship game to lead Memphis to the league championship, and earned game MVP honors as well, becoming the first non-American to win championship MVP and the first player in Summer League history to win both honors.<ref>{{cite news|title=Clarke stakes Grizzlies to summer league crown|date=July 15, 2019|website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27199181 |access-date=July 16, 2019}}</ref>

On October 23, 2019, Clarke made his NBA debut, coming off the bench in a 101–120 loss to the [[Miami Heat]] with eight points, seven rebounds, an assist and a block.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160629|title=Butler misses Miami debut, Heat beat Grizzlies 120-101|date=October 23, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 23, 2019}}</ref> On December 18, he scored a career-high 27 points, alongside seven rebounds, in a 122–126 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=THUNDER OVERCOME 24-POINT DEFICIT TO BEAT GRIZZLIES 126-122 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900412 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Clarke again scored 27 points, alongside six rebounds and two steals, in a 111–104 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CLARKE LEADS GRIZZLIES TO A 111-104 WIN OVER TRAIL BLAZERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900812 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Clarke participated in the 2020 [[Rising Stars Challenge]], where he had 22 points and eight rebounds.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28693666 |title=NBA All-Star 2020: Grading Zion Williamson, Luka Doncic and every player in the Rising Stars |work=ESPN.com |date=2020-02-14 |access-date=2026-05-13 |last=Pelton |first=Kevin}}</ref> On February 25, 2020, it was announced that Clarke would be sidelined because of a right [[quadriceps]] injury.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/2020/2/25/21153763/brandon-clarke-out-with-leg-injury-nba-memphis-grizzlies-news |title=Brandon Clarke out with leg injury |date=February 25, 2020 |website=grizzlybearblues.com |access-date=March 16, 2020 |archive-date=December 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201201071402/https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/2020/2/25/21153763/brandon-clarke-out-with-leg-injury-nba-memphis-grizzlies-news |url-status=dead}}</ref> On September 15, Clarke was named to the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20]] [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/09/15/nba-2019-20-all-rookie-first-team-official-release |title=Ja Morant, Zion Williamsom headline 2019-20 Kia All-Rookie First Team Tyler Herro, Rui Hachimura voted to Second Team |date=September 15, 2020 |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 15, 2020}}</ref>

On December 16, 2020, the Grizzlies exercised their team option on Clarke for the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies exercise 2021-22 contract options on Ja Morant, Jaren Jackson Jr., Brandon Clarke and Grayson Allen|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-exercise-2021-22-contract-options-on-ja-morant-jaren-jackson-jr-brandon-clarke-and-grayson-allen-201216|date=December 16, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 16, 2020}}</ref> On January 8, 2021, he scored a season-high 21 points, alongside eight rebounds, five assists and two blocks, in a 115–110 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BROOKS LEADS GRIZZLIES TO 1ST HOME VICTORY 115-110 OVER NETS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000128 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Clarke was named to the World Team for the 2021 Rising Stars Challenge, but the game was not played due to limitations caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2021-nba-rising-stars-zion-williamson-lamelo-ball-headline-list-of-players-selected-for-usa-world-rosters/ |title=2021 NBA Rising Stars: Zion Williamson, LaMelo Ball headline list of players selected for USA, World rosters |work=CBS Sports |date=2021-03-04 |access-date=2026-05-13 |last=Wimbish |first=Jasmyn}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/allstar/NBA_2021_rookie.html |title=2021 NBA Rising Stars |work=Basketball Reference}}</ref> The Grizzlies qualified for the postseason for the first time since [[2017 NBA playoffs|2017]] after a series of [[NBA Play-In Tournament|play-in tournament]] wins. On May 29, during the Grizzlies' first round series against the [[Utah Jazz]], Clarke made his playoff debut, playing seven minutes and grabbing one rebound in a 111–121 game 3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MITCHELL SCORES 29 POINTS, JAZZ BEAT GRIZZLIES FOR 2-1 LEAD |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000143 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Grizzlies were eliminated by the Jazz in five games.
[[File:Brandon Clarke (51814063744) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Clarke with the Grizzlies in 2022]]
On October 16, 2021, the Grizzlies exercised their team option on Clarke for the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies exercise rookie options for Morant, Clarke, Bane|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/grizzlies-exercise-rookie-options-morant-clarke-bane/|access-date=2022-01-13|website=Sportsnet.ca|language=en}}</ref> On January 28, 2022, Clarke scored a season-high 22 points, alongside three rebounds, in a 119–109 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ALL-STAR MORANT HAS TRIPLE-DOUBLE, GRIZZLIES BEAT JAZZ |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100740 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Grizzlies qualified for the playoffs for the second straight season, where they faced the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] during their first round series. On April 26, Clarke recorded playoff career highs of 21 points and 15 rebounds in a 111–109 game 5 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MORANT'S LAST-SECOND LAYUP GIVES GRIZZLIES 3-2 SERIES LEAD |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100155 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 29, he recorded 17 points, eleven rebounds, five assists and three blocks as the Grizzlies eliminated the Timberwolves from the playoffs with a 114–106 game 6 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GRIZZLIES RALLY AGAIN PAST WOLVES 114-106 TO REACH 2ND ROUND |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100156 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Grizzlies were eventually eliminated during the second round, with the [[Golden State Warriors]] beating them in six games.

On October 16, 2022, Clarke signed a four-year, $52 million contract extension with the Grizzlies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Brandon Clarke to multi-year contract extension |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-brandon-clarke-to-multi-year-contract-extension |access-date=February 4, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandon Clarke, Grizzlies Agree to 4-Year, $52M Contract Extension |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10052588-brandon-clarke-grizzlies-agree-to-4-year-52m-contract-extension |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> On March 3, 2023, during a 113–97 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]], he suffered a left leg injury and exited the game after playing only two minutes. The next day, the Grizzlies announced that Clarke had suffered a [[Achilles tendon rupture|torn left Achilles]], ending his 2022–23 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grizzlies PR on Twitter: "The @memgrizz announced the following medical update" |url=https://twitter.com/GrizzliesPR/status/1632097861222498307 |access-date=March 4, 2023 |website=Twitter}}</ref>

Clarke made 64 appearances (18 starts) for the Grizzlies during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 8.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 1.0 assists. On March 22, 2025, Clarke was ruled out for the remainder of the season after suffering a high-grade [[posterior cruciate ligament injury|PCL sprain]] in his right knee.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke to avoid surgery on knee|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44481342/grizzlies-forward-brandon-clarke-avoid-surgery-knee|access-date=April 3, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> 

On September 26, 2025, it was announced that Clarke would require an [[arthroscopy|arthroscopic]] procedure to address knee [[synovitis]], which was suffered during offseason training.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brandon Clarke set for knee procedure; Jackson, Edey to ramp up|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46389080/sources-grizzlies-brandon-clarke-set-knee-procedure|access-date=January 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He played in only two games for Memphis during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 4.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 0.5 assists. On March 24, 2026, Clarke was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to a right calf strain.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' Ja Morant out for season due to elbow injury|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/grizzlies-ja-morant-season-due-120730086.html|access-date=June 7, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
In 2025, Clarke started a charity, the Brandon Clarke Foundation, whose efforts included supporting ARISE2Read, a nonprofit focused on literacy and mentorship, and hosting events for youth in Memphis.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/never-star-brandon-clarkes-journey-110005821.html|title=Never the star, Brandon Clarke's journey with Grizzlies reflected selflessness|author= Cole, Damichael|work=Memphis Commercial Appeal|date=May 15, 2026}}</ref>

On April 1, 2026, Clarke was arrested in [[Cross County, Arkansas]], for possession of a controlled substance ({{convert|235.6|g|disp=sqbr}} of [[kratom]], a [[Controlled Substances Act#Schedule I|schedule 1 controlled substance]] in Arkansas), fleeing and exceeding the speed limit (over {{convert|100|mph|disp=sqbr}}), and [[Illegal drug trade|trafficking]] a controlled substance.<ref>{{cite web|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48372917|title=Grizzlies' Clarke arrested in Arkansas on drug, speeding charges|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=April 1, 2026|access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.actionnews5.com/2026/04/02/grizzlies-clarke-led-deputies-100mph-chase-sheriff-says|title=Grizzlies' Clarke led deputies on 100mph chase, sheriff says Grizzlies' Clarke led deputies on 100mph chase, sheriff says|date=April 2, 2026|access-date=May 12, 2026|agency=[[WMC-TV]]|last1=Gallant|first1=Jacob|last2=Montgomery|first2=Garner}}</ref> While he was released on a $25,000 [[bail|bond]], Clarke was scheduled to appear at an arraignment hearing on May 15 at the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas|St. Francis County District Court]] in [[Forrest City, Arkansas]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Vardon |last2=Clark |last3=Gutierrez |title=Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke dies at 29. 'A warm, kind spirit.'|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7273558/2026/05/12/brandon-clarke-grizzlies-dead/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times Company]] |date=May 12, 2026 |access-date=May 12, 2026|first=Joe|first2=Christian|first3=Melody|name-list-style=and}}</ref>

Clarke died on May 11, 2026, in [[Los Angeles]], California, at the age of 29.<ref name="NBC2026">{{cite news |last=Broad |first=Dennis |date=May 12, 2026 |title=29-year-old Memphis Grizzlies player Brandon Clarke dies in the San Fernando Valley |url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/memphis-grizzlies-player-brandon-clarke-dies-at-29/3889534/ |work=[[NBC News]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Statement on the passing of Brandon Clarke|url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/rumors/2026/05/12/statement-on-the-passing-of-brandon-clarke/90047550007/|date=May 12, 2026|access-date=May 12, 2026|website=HoopsHype|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=May 12, 2026|title=Grizzlies' Brandon Clarke has died at age 29|url=https://www.fox13memphis.com/news/grizzlies-brandon-clarke-has-died-at-age-29/article_804c83cb-aa2d-46f0-8bfc-b78b09f83f70.html|agency=[[WHBQ-TV|Fox 13]]|access-date=May 12, 2026}}</ref> His cause of death was confirmed almost three months later to be an [[overdose|accidental overdose]] of cocaine, heroin, and the combined effects of multiple other [[prescription drugs|presciption medications]], otherwise known as [[Speedball (drug)|speedball]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49555855/coroner-finds-grizzlies-brandon-clarke-died-effects-cocaine-heroin|title=Coroner: Grizzlies' Brandon Clarke died from effects of cocaine, heroin|author= Tom Schad|date=August 7, 2026}}</ref> <ref>{{cite web|url=https://me.lacounty.gov/case-detail/?caseNumber=2026-07644|title=Los Angeles Medical Examiner - Brandon Clarke|date=August 7, 2026}}</ref>
